language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, I am Tim.

Hi! I’m Peter. And this is my mom. She is looking into a telescope because she’s an astrophysicist. We are in Antarctica, at a research center. My mom looks at the stars all night. Because of the coldness at night, the sky is very clear.
Stars come from huge clouds of dust and gas, called Nebulae. These stars grow big and then collapse. If a star is larger than the sun when it collapses, a supernova occurs.
A supernova is a large explosion from which a neutron star or a black hole is formed, marking the end of this star’s life cycle. A black hole won’t allow anything to escape its pull.
When a star is about the same size as the sun when it collapses, a white dwarf is formed. A white dwarf is the cooling remains of a star, and it glows faintly.
After a long time, the white dwarf becomes a black dwarf, no longer glowing, and marking the final stage of the star’s life cycle.

My mom teaches me many different things about stars; the different groups, their characteristics and their life cycles. Their life cycle is so fascinating! Stars are formed from gas clouds, called Nebulae, and burn for a very long time. They shine bright and give off energy for millions of years, before they collapse. Finally they die.
And do you see the posters with the stars on it? I made those. To make them, I need a lot of information. Will you help me to get to know everything about the moon and the stars?
It is awesome that we can help you, Peter! Let's go!

Hi! I’m making a poster about constellations for my room. Constellations are formed by groups of stars. I can’t remember some names for some of these constellations. Can you help me?

My mom told me that constellations are named after shapes or Gods from Greek Mythology. For example, Sagittarius was an archer, so his constellation is in the shape of an archer. The Summer Triangle is in the shape of a triangle, Cassiopeia is in the shape of a stretchy “W”, and Orion can be recognized by his ‘belt’, which has 3 stars. Can you guess which one is the Big Dipper?

Hi! My mom told me that nuclear fusion causes stars to shine bright and produce energy. They are large and made mostly of hydrogen and helium. She told me that the color of a star changes with its temperature and stars are classified in four ways: by color, temperature, size and how bright they are. Can you help me answer these questions?
